subject: gk
question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states that ‘The Directive Principles of State Policy are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply the Principles in making laws’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 37**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 37** of the Indian Constitution specifies that the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• It mandates that it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• Although the DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, they are crucial for governance.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The Directive Principles act as guidelines to the central and state governments of India to frame laws and policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**:

 
 
• DPSPs are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Article 36 to Article 51.
 
• These principles have been inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland.
 
• The aim is to establish a just society in India, and they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciable Nature**:
 
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• However, they are considered essential for the understanding and governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Categories of DPSPs**:
 
 
• DPSPs are classified into three categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual.
 
• Socialistic principles aim at providing social and economic justice.
 
• Gandhian principles reflect the vision of Mahatma Gandhi for a self-sufficient village economy.
 
• Liberal-Intellectual principles are based on liberal ideals of justice, liberty, and equality.
 
 
 
• **Relation with Fundamental Rights**:
 
 
• There has been a debate on the relationship between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs.
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable and legally enforceable, while DPSPs are not.
 
• However, the Supreme Court of India has often interpreted Fundamental Rights and DPSPs harmoniously.
